content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: move 4 cross-skilled agents from general to payments now and run outage messaging, callbacks and chat deflection. It is the only plan that reaches the 80% target, at 81.1% for 12:15-14:15, for ₹636.","why":"The spike is caused by the P1 UPI switch incident (INC-20261006-6998), not by staffing. We have 42 of 43 agents on shift and handle time is below forecast. Payments calls ran 90% over forecast at 10:30, and upi_payment_failed calls are 2.56x normal. R2 tackles both sides. On supply, it moves 4 agents to payments from 12:15 to 13:00 and delays breaks on both queues by 45 minutes. On demand, it adds the IVR outage message, callbacks and 20% chat deflection. Predicted service level over the disruption window is 81.1% (payments 78.5%, general 85.6%). Abandon rate falls to 5.4%, against 8.9% with no action. Rest of day is 89.2%. No overtime is used, which respects today's zero budget, and there are no policy violations.","trade_offs":["Cost: R2 costs ₹636. R1 and P3 cost ₹480 but stop at 77.1% and 76.7%, short of the target. P1 costs nothing but reaches only 70.0%.","Other queue: general gives up 4 agents early and has breaks delayed by 45 minutes, yet is still predicted at 85.6%, the best of any plan. The risk to general looks low.","Customer impact: some payments and general callers will hear the outage message, be offered a callback or be pushed to chat instead of reaching an agent.","Payments itself is predicted at 78.5%, just under 80%. The overall target is met only because general is performing strongly."],"watch":"Watch payments service level and abandons between 12:15 and 13:00 while the 4 agents are moved, and check that general holds once its breaks are delayed. Keep tracking the UPI incident status. If the outage runs past 14:15, or the outage message and deflection pull less volume than expected, the payments shortfall will widen. Since overtime is not available, the next step would be to involve the duty manager."}
